steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I see. You sought your friend's family for her, and so came from shy a myriad li away to Yan. Admirable indeed.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: However, Mount Hui-ch'i? And Kou-wu City? I've never heard of any cities like it in the vicinity... But this place isn't far from Mount Sky. Perhaps it's a small peak I know not the name of. The possibility is there.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Eh? Mount Sky...?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Well, this is annoying.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Sorry, could I ask which part of Yan we're in right now?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: This place is at the edge of Mount P'o, its name is P'o-shan Village.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: (I've never heard of it, absolutely never heard of it!)

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: O—okay, then, what's the current year...?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: The year is Ching-tso 7, currently the Beginning of Spring, with the Dusk Ridding just passed.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: (Quietly) Ching-tso?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: (Quietly) Benefactor, I won't mince words: my history is quite poor, but Ching-tso... has to be centuries ago at least. I've never heard of an era by that name...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: (Quietly) Wh... what's going on, benefactor? Could we have tumbled a thousand years back when we opened that door?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: (Quietly) Did they have gardens and buildings like this a thousand years ago?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: (Quietly) Of course they couldn't! Perhaps this Umbrella-Boiling Hermit blurted out pure nonsense? But I can't imagine he'd do that, noting how refined his manner is.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Heroes three, you've come to our aid. You are my honored guests. If you have any questions, ask them forthright; you needn't refrain.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Could we trouble you to tell us about the culture and customs here? To be honest, this place isn't where we thought we were going. It seems we went astray, and we're sort of at a loss.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: For... for example, tell us about this village?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Ah... there is much to tell of the origins of P'o-shan Village. Story has it that seventy years ago, a great fire started on a rich merchant's property, bringing untold calamity.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: The rich merchant was frightened, and planned to leave, to find a place where nature blessed treasured lands, so he could live out the rest of his days.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Subsequently, in the midst of all the ashes, the people of his village found a peculiar painting on the ground...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Painting?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Correct. The house had burned to the ground, yet that painting scroll remained unharmed, and after brushing off the ash, it was as good as new.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: The merchant heard of the painting, dove deep into his pockets to buy it back once again, seeking good luck to ward against fires.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: In his new residence, the more the merchant gazed into the scenery in the painting, the more he took an interest. He sent out hundreds of servants in search of the marvelous feng shui this scroll had portrayed—

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: —and so came here, and so this village, and this garden came to be.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Was that your ancestor?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Not so, not so. The world's affairs are never constant. Decades in the past, after the merchant's death, his few sons in their incompetence frittered away the household's wealth.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: By chance, my father had some spare money from a string of opportune coincidences, and so bought the gardens and settled down here.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Afterwards, as nearby Catastrophes were infrequent and the mountains and rivers gorgeous, many talented scholars were drawn here, and over time, P'o-shan Village became as it is today.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: (I mean, it sounds wonderful.)

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: (No issues with it yet, I think...)

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: So, the color of the sky...?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: The what?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Uh, I mean, daytime and nighttime seem to be mixed together...

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: We've always worked as the sun rose, and rested as it set. What doubts might you have?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: It's been two hours since the bell sounded... with the twelve-branch double-hour system, it'd be one of those. The sun's hasn't moved at all. What's causing that?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: The sun? Move?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: The sun and moon sit in the sky, sun in the east, moon in the west, eternally unchanging. What other position would they assume?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Hm? You all have a peculiar look on your faces. Have I said something improper?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Er, benefactors, if I could interrupt, just very quickly.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: May I dare ask, will you again be telling stories here the next day?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Naturally.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: As that is the case tomorrow, I presume yesterday you also took up your hand fan and gavel block?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I lay at home, with the collection of strange tales as my one and only hobby, naught but the art of storytelling to pass the time. Thus, every day, at the Hour of Shen, changing for nothing.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Err. Then with the sun and moon constant above, and 'today, the next day, and yesterday,' how should you define what one 'day' is?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: You're quite the jokester, Brother No. Twelve earthly branches make up one day. Need you ask?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Erm... do the twelve branches and the twenty-four hours not track the time over one day and night?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Hmm? How mystifying. I wonder just where you all came from? The twelve branches indicate the necessary periods between the sun rising above the earth in the far east, and the moon above the mountains in the far west, don't they?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Of course, they also indicate how this road is partitioned. East to west, P'o-shan Village lies from the late-morn sixth to the late-eve twelfth.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I've heard tell of mountains beyond mountains. Could it be that beyond Mount Hung-tung and downstream of the Tung-shêng River, other places are not so?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Then... suppose P'o-shan Village alone occupies such a vast domain; if there are villages elsewhere, mightn't they be forever without daylight?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Or they'd be stuck in the day, and they'd never even sleep properly. Sucks to be them.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: This... this, I am truly unclear on.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Have you never left this village before? Aren't there any other travelers here?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I never have. Very few people have ever come here, and of the youth that leave, very few ever return.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I must confess, the 'Yan' we presently know is from the library the rich merchant left behind, and nothing more.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Has a Catastrophe never struck this place before?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: They're just as rare. At least apart from the ancient records, our three generations have never seen one before.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: And so, we hardly leave the bounds of P'o-shan Village. And just as you see, scarcely any travelers come here, let alone any officials or Messengers or other such persons.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: To say P'o-shan Village is presently cut off from the outside world would be no exaggeration at all. That said, only when you disregard the affairs of the world can you be content.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: And the monsters?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Ah... I know not when it began. Come every Dusk Ridding, Mount Hung-tung often bears monsters that come to disturb the village, over perhaps three to five days. For so many unbroken years, it has been this way.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: In these years, I've turned every record over, asked the very few strangers whenever I could, and I've never found any way to address it...

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: But as long as you hide somewhere the sun is, those monsters won't come near.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Versus braving the dangers and battling them 'til one side is dead, much better is finding peace and safety, hiding under the sun, passing not a night and staying vigil throughout...

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Over time, it's become a usual practice of ours here.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Dear me! And I thought this place was a true peach-blossom utopia! I hadn't imagined such troubles here... Those monsters are much too frightening. To give them a wide berth is the sensible thing!

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: (Quietly) Benefactors, their ways are plainly much too strange...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Sir, one last question.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: You know that we came here to look for someone. I have a, uh, token. Could you take a look?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: This is...?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Hoh...

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Craft to surpass Nature.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: However... most regretfully, if I'd ever seen such an unusual item as this before, I'd certainly—

steps.name: Villager
steps.text: Sir, the feast is prepared.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Good, good. May I ask you all if you've found anywhere to stay in the village?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Not for the time being...

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: You've arrived as guests. It'd be best if you rested here for some days, and once the Dusk Ridding has passed, you hurry on your way again!

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: (Quietly) Benefactor, your verdict?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: (Quietly) It's not like we've got anywhere to go... We may as well stay in the village for now and gather intel.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: (Quietly) This place obviously doesn't match up with the 'Yan' we know. Not to mention, we still have no indication of how we got here...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Right!

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: In that case, we'd be best to accept.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: So in the end, we still don't have a literal clue... Eh, but the tea here smells great. Is this how the green tea is in Yan?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Kroos!

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Don't worry, I've got my manners.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: I could drink this.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: They've put out fruits here...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Ah, are you testing for poison, benefactors? You should've said sooner; let me come to your aid!

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Hey...!

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Mmph!

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Mm, dear benefactor, this fruit is quite fresh! And peculiarly sweet.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: I didn't mean...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Mind it not! As the proverb goes, one cannot lack the heart to protect, no?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: I wasn't worried if they poisoned anything... I was just checking through... everything in our perimeter.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: You're pretty fidgety right now, aren't you? No problem, we're all the same. Lost in the fog.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: It's like we're checking if we're even still alive.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Checking again, huh?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: You chill here. I still need to take another look outside.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: How could I leave my benefactor to toil alone! I must accompany you!

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Then let's split up and move. The way things are, none of us is gonna sit still.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Alright. Then shall we meet in... two hours?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Do you think we can trust him?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Even if it's not rare to see poor bastards in a tight spot on the wastes, coincidences like his are the last thing you can trust.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: I think so too. And it's a fact that he's been deceiving us.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Gloompincers that leave their nests are highly aggressive. And when we found him, he was up in a tree looking all sad... but he was about 800 whole meters away from the car crash.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: And just seeing his actions...

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Even if he's got no ill will, we've still gotta be wary of each other.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: I'll keep an eye on him.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: *Sigh*.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: (I may have been drawn into something indescribably bizarre... But I suppose that has had a silver lining...)

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: (Speaking of which, this truly isn't—any joking matter... If I can't find a way to return, then what do I even do...)

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: (Oh... but Lava and Kroos have been quite the saviors to me. I can't fault them for this... *sigh*! I'll just have to see as I go—)

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Ohh, my apologies there, I'm truly sorry. I was lost in thought and clearly wasn't watching my way—

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: By your appearance, surely you are from outside, are you not? It has been so long since I saw a visitor!

steps.name: Saga
steps.text: I am Saga, humble servant of the Buddha, a wandering monk from Higashi! May I ask from whence thou comest?
